The fix is straightforward. The original code only replaced non-alphanumeric characters with `-`, but didn't handle:
1. Multiple consecutive hyphens (e.g., `"hello--world"`)
2. Leading/trailing hyphens (e.g., `"hello-world-"`)

I added two lines after the substitution:
- `re.sub(r"-{2,}", "-", text)` collapses multiple hyphens into one
- `text.strip("-")` removes leading/trailing hyphens

This makes `slugify("Hello,  World!")` return `"hello-world"` and `slugify("--a--b--")` return `"a-b"`, while preserving the public signature.

arguments.summary: Fixed `slugify` in `textkit/slug.py` by adding two post-processing steps: collapsing multiple consecutive hyphens into one (`re.sub(r"-{2,}", "-", text)`) and stripping leading/trailing hyphens (`text.strip("-")`). This ensures `slugify("Hello,  World!")` returns `"hello-world"` and `slugify("--a--b--")` returns `"a-b"`.
